extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for submitting, timing, content, and handling of Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 during USPTO patent prosecution. Covers deadlines, required statements/fees, exceptions (RCE/CPA/QPIDS), and examiner procedures for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing windows for IDS filing (four-stage framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDS filing rules are linked to four stages: (1) within three months of filing (or before mailing of first Office action on the merits) for national apps, or analogous measures for international and design apps; (2) after (1) but before prosecution closes (before final Office action, Notice of Allowance, or Ex parte Quayle); (3) after (2) but on or before payment of issue fee; (4) after (3) up to the time the application can be effectively withdrawn from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed subrules: for national applications (including continuations/CIPs but not CPAs) the three-month measure is from actual filing date; for international national-stage entry the three months runs from entry date under 37 CFR 1.491; for international design apps the three months runs from publication under Hague Agreement Article 10(3). An IDS filed within one of these (first) periods requires neither a fee nor a statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e). An IDS is considered filed on the day received in the Office or earlier mailing date if accompanied by a properly executed certificate of mailing/fax or compliant Priority Mail Express under 37 CFR 1.8/1.10. If the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday, filing on the next business day is timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed within three-month window will be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: All IDSs that comply with the content requirements of 37 CFR 1.98 and are filed within three months of the filing date (or analogous starting date) will be considered by the examiner, regardless of other events in the examination up to that point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, even if a final Office action, notice of allowance, or Ex parte Quayle action is mailed prior to three months from filing, a complete IDS filed within the three-month window will be considered. 'Action on the merits' is any action treating patentability (e.g., rejections or allowability indications), not merely formal/procedural correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special RCE and CPA timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-month window described above does not apply to RCEs filed under 37 CFR 1.114 or to CPAs filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d). An IDS filed after the filing of an RCE or CPA will be considered if filed before the mailing date of a first Office action on the merits in that prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because an RCE makes the application an amended application with short turnover, applicants are encouraged to file any IDS with the RCE; likewise applicants should file IDSs in CPAs as early as possible, preferably with the CPA request. If an IDS cannot be filed before the first Office action on the merits after an RCE/CPA, applicant may request a three-month suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(b)/(c) and is requested to make a courtesy call when an IDS is mailed shortly before the suspension expires. See MPEP § 706.07(h) for RCE details.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after period (1) but before prosecution closes: statement or fee required (37 CFR 1.97(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed after the initial three-month/first-action window but prior to the prosecution closing (i.e., before final Office action, Notice of Allowance, or Ex parte Quayle) will be considered only if accompanied by either (1) a statement as specified in 37 CFR 1.97(e) or (2) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed with a 1.97(e) statement and information is used in a new ground of rejection on unamended claims, the next Office action will not be made final because the applicant submitted the information promptly. However, a final rejection is appropriate if the new ground was necessitated by an amendment by applicant. If the IDS is filed with the fee, the examiner may use the information and make the next Office action final provided no other new ground not necessitated by amendment is introduced. If a final/allowance/Q action was mailed and later withdrawn, the application is treated as not having had such a mailing for IDS-consideration timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed on/after final action but before or simultaneous with issue fee: statement and fee required (37 CFR 1.97(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed on or after the mailing date of a final action, notice of allowance, or an action that closes prosecution but before or simultaneous with payment of the issue fee will be considered only if accompanied by both (A) a statement as specified in 37 CFR 1.97(e) and (B) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements reflect the advanced stage of prosecution; payment of the fee and submission of the appropriate statement are essential for consideration, assuming the IDS also meets 37 CFR 1.98 content requirements. Form paragraph 6.52 may be used to notify applicant the IDS is being considered when filed after prosecution has been closed but before issue fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after payment of the issue fee generally not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: After the issue fee has been paid, information disclosure statements filed in the application will not be considered and will merely be placed in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may pursue alternatives to have information considered: file a petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c) to withdraw application from issue (with stringent requirements and timing uncertainties), file an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114, or file a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b)/(d). The Quick Path IDS (QPIDS) pilot program (under specific circumstances) may allow submission after issue-fee-but-prior-to-grant — see USPTO QPIDS materials. Petitions under 1.313(c)(1) to withdraw from issue require an unequivocal statement that one or more claims are unpatentable over the information (a statement that only a 'serious question' exists is insufficient).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content and format under 37 CFR 1.98
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must comply with the content/format requirements of 37 CFR 1.98, including a separate paper listing all patents, publications, applications, or other information submitted and legible copies of each cited foreign patent document, each non-patent literature publication (or the relevant portion), and all other information (or the relevant portion) that caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A listing of references in the specification is not a proper IDS (37 CFR 1.98(b) requires a separate paper). If the format or copy requirements are not met, the information need not be considered by the examiner. Where an item fails to comply with all requirements, that item will not be considered (draw a line through it) but other compliant items may be considered. If none of the information is considered, the examiner should write 'not considered' on the IDS form and draw a diagonal line or 'X' across PTO/SB/08A and 08B and make the form of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e): two alternative formulations and strict meaning requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e) must state either (1) that each item was first cited in a communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to filing the statement, or (2) that no item was cited in a communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application and, to the signer's knowledge after making reasonable inquiry, no item was known to any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) more than three months prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either of the two alternative statements may be used; the exact language of 1.97(e)(1)/(2) is strongly encouraged but not required so long as the meaning is identical — varying language risks nonacceptance. The date on the foreign communication begins the three-month period (use the mailing date if two dates present). A 'counterpart foreign patent application' requires priority or substantively identical disclosures; a PCT international application designating the US is not a counterpart for this purpose. Multiple lists/statements may be included in one IDS, but applicant should expressly designate which statement applies to which citation(s). A copy of the foreign search report is not required with a 1.97(e) statement, but an English-language version may be submitted to satisfy concise explanation needs for non-English citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'after making reasonable inquiry' for 1.97(e)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person signing a 1.97(e)(2) statement must, after making reasonable inquiry, have a basis for the assertion that no item was known to any individual with a duty to disclose more than three months prior to filing the statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered practitioner may rely on client statements about dates, but if a client provides information without addressing when it was known, the practitioner must make reasonable inquiry before signing. If an inventor provided a publication to counsel with intent to cite it, counsel should ask when the inventor became aware before making a 1.97(e)(2) statement. The statement may be based on present, good-faith knowledge without a file search. A 1.97(e) statement need not be an oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.68; a practitioner’s statement that the IDS was filed within the three-month period will be accepted absent evidence to the contrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign office communications and family-member English patents treated as citations for 1.97(e)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications from foreign patent offices that list a family of patents (including US or other English-language patents) may allow the US/English-language patent from the family list to be construed as being cited by the foreign patent office for purposes of 1.97(e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should consider the related US or other English-language patent if 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 are complied with. A dated foreign-office communication by itself will not substitute for the required 1.97(e)(1) statement unless it clearly shows the IDS is within three months of the cited communication and that the items were 'first cited' in that communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions of time for filing an IDS (37 CFR 1.97(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: No extensions of time for filing an information disclosure statement are permitted under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide attempt is made to comply with 37 CFR 1.98 but part of the required content is inadvertently omitted, additional time may be given to enable full compliance (i.e., limited discretion where inadvertent omission occurred).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of noncomplying IDS (placement in file but not considered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.97(i), information submitted before grant that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 will be placed in the file but will not be considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an IDS does not comply with time-based requirements (including lacking required fee or statement), the IDS will be placed in the file and not considered; applicant may resubmit or correct deficiencies but the submission date of the corrected/new IDS will be the operative date for timing compliance. Examiner should notify applicant of noncompliance and reasons using form paragraphs 6.49–6.49.10 (examples provided). If an item in an IDS fails to comply with requirements, draw a line through that citation to show it was not considered while leaving compliant citations for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph and marking procedures for 'not considered' IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an IDS is not considered, the examiner should use form paragraph 6.49 (and its subparagraphs) to inform applicant of noncompliance and reasons; if none of the citations on PTO/SB/08A and 08B are considered, draw a diagonal line or 'X' across the form and make it of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific form paragraphs cover common reasons (e.g., 6.49.01: lacks 1.97(e) statement after first action; 6.49.02: lacks fee after first action; 6.49.03/6.49.05: lacks statement/fee after prosecution closed and before issue fee payment; 6.49.06: references listed in specification rather than separate IDS paper; 6.49.07: no copy of references). Use form PTOL-90 or PTO-90C for IDS submitted after issue fee paid (¶13.09 example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial compliance: crossing out noncompliant items and considering compliant ones
rubrics_metrics.description: If some items in an IDS comply with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 and others do not, the examiner will not consider the noncompliant items (draw a line through them) but will consider the items that do comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information was listed in the specification instead of on a separate paper (impermissible format), the information need not be considered unless the examiner has cited those references on form PTO-892. The examiner should notify applicant in the next Office action that the improperly submitted information was not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of IDS submission on finality of next Office action when IDS used in new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If information submitted during the period governed by 37 CFR 1.97(c) with a 1.97(e) statement is used in a new ground of rejection on unamended claims, the next Office action will not be made final because it is clear applicant submitted the information promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, the information submitted with a 1.97(e) statement may be used and the next Office action made final if the new ground of rejection was necessitated by an amendment of the application by applicant. If the IDS was filed with the fee under 1.17(p) in this period, the examiner may use the information and make the next Office action final provided no other new ground not necessitated by amendment is introduced.
